claim: The Forge upgrades, re-rolls, sockets and breaks down — and asks before it does anything you cannot undo.
evidence: src/IdleXIdle.Game/ForgeScreen.cs:1684-1718 (DoRefine) takes the cost and rolls Forge.TryRefine with no question asked. Forge.cs:39-44 and 246-252: from the 6th upgrade an upgrade can slip (6%, rising to 60%). Forge.cs:280-292: a slip drops the item one level and one upgrade, and the cost is not refunded. ForgeScreen.cs:1647 (DoReforgeEnchant) replaces the enchant with no question either. The game asks only before sell, salvage, junk and crush gem (ForgeScreen.cs:891-893, 1508, 1551, 1583, 3524), and the player can turn that question off (AskBeforeScrap, ForgeScreen.cs:1127). The only exception is a worn item. The tab labels are UPGRADE / RE-ROLL / SOCKET / SALVAGE (ForgeScreen.cs:736). The same wrong sentence is in docs/store/itch/description.html.
replacement: The Forge upgrades, re-rolls, sockets gems and salvages. It asks before you sell or salvage an item, and before you set or crush a gem. From the sixth upgrade on, an upgrade can slip and drop the item one level and one step. The button shows the chance of success first.
note: Confirmed. DoRefine (ForgeScreen.cs:1684-1718) charges the player and rolls Forge.TryRefine without asking. From the 6th upgrade a slip is possible (6% rising to 60%, Forge.cs:41-44, 246-252), it drops the item one level and one upgrade step, and the cost is not refunded (Forge.cs:276-292). DoReforgeEnchant (1647) replaces the enchant without asking. Only sell, salvage and junk ask (and the player can turn that off with AskBeforeScrap, 1127; a worn item always asks), plus setting a gem (_socketAsk, 1139, 3478) and crushing a gem (3524). The tab labels are UPGRADE / RE-ROLL / SOCKET / SALVAGE (736). The proposed replacement is close but has two gaps. It misses that setting a gem also asks, although setting a gem destroys nothing. It also says a slip drops 'one level', but a slip drops one level AND one step; the game's own line is 'A SLIP DROPS ONE LEVEL AND ONE STEP'. description.html has the same wrong sentence.

It then starts the exe once and stops if the title does not draw. Last, it runs `butler push <folder> <target>:windows --userversion <sha> --if-changed`, so the git sha is the build version. note: Confirmed. claim: Weave skills from Source × Style × Vow — 6 sources, 6 styles, 13 vows
evidence: The numbers are right: 6 sources (Sources/Source.cs:19), 6 styles (Builds/SkillCatalogue.cs:34-53) and 13 vows (Builds/Vows.cs:441-599). The model is wrong. Skills are no longer built from a Source and a style: 'A slot used to BE a Source and a Form, and the skill was composed from the pair; the Form column died' (Builds/PlayerLoadout.cs:28-32). A skill is now a fixed catalogue entry, and its chosen variation carries the Source (SkillCatalogue.cs:120-125). Vows are a separate layer and not part of a skill.
replacement: - Weave a build from 12 shared skills in 6 styles, plus each champion's own skill. A skill's chosen variation gives it one of 6 sources. 13 vows to take on.
note: Confirmed. The counts are right: 6 sources (Source.cs:19) and 13 vows (13 vow ids in Vows.cs). The 'Source x Style x Vow' model is wrong. A skill is a fixed catalogue entry with a fixed style, and its Source comes from the variation you choose (SkillVariation.Source; PlayerLoadout.cs:28-32 says 'the Form column died'). So you cannot pair any source with any style. There are also 10 signature skills, one per champion (SkillCatalogue.cs:809-1105), which the bullet leaves out. The proposed replacement ends with a loose fragment, '13 vows.'; the corrected text below fixes that.

claim: The build is two active + two passive slots (a fifth on the trait spine), three keystones, and Vows

Progression/Unlocks.cs:286-290 says 'Four slots is where it STOPS ... the trait tree used to sell a fifth, and it no longer does.' The trait tree itself is deleted (Prestige/MemoryDustWallet.cs:10-15). This line is outside the Status paragraph, but it is in the same README.

note: Confirmed. Build.SkillSlots = 4, and the comment says 'The fifth slot is removed' (Build.cs:256-261). SlotCapacity is capped at 4 with 'there is no longer anything in the game that sells a fifth' (284-287). Unlocks.cs:286-288 agrees, and the trait tree is deleted. claim: Skill points come from depth (respec free); trait points from conquest and mastery (permanent); learned skills are learned for good.
evidence: Trait points are gone: 'TRAIT POINTS are gone with the tree ... nothing spends them now' (Prestige/MemoryDustWallet.cs:28-31, also Progression/Unlocks.cs:72-77). Traits are awakened by play (Traits/TraitCatalogue.cs, 26 entries). The depth points are called MASTERY points (Builds/MasteryPoints.cs:36-46; UI line 'Earn three mastery points by going deeper', Unlocks.cs:221). Learned skills are NOT kept for good any more. Builds/MasteryTree.cs:145-155 says the permanent _learned set was removed ('ACCESS IS TEMPORARY. EXPERIENCE IS PERMANENT.'). AvailableSkills (MasteryTree.cs:317) is exactly what the taken nodes teach, so a refunded road takes the skill away. Only the skill's levels stay (SkillProgress.cs:18-22). This line is outside the Status paragraph.
replacement: - **Nothing resets.** Six regions conquered in a chain, then the Corruption ratchets. Mastery points come from depth, and taking them back is free. Traits are awakened by play and never bought. A skill keeps its levels for good, even when you take it off or give its road back.
note: Confirmed on all three points. (1) Trait points are gone (MemoryDustWallet.cs:28-31). UnlockFacts now counts TraitsDiscovered (Unlocks.cs:71-77). (2) Depth pays mastery points (MasteryPoints.FromDepth; UI text 'Earn three mastery points by going deeper'), and respec is free (MasteryTree.cs:135, Respec/Refund). (3) Learned skills are not kept for good. MasteryTree removed _learned ('ACCESS IS TEMPORARY. EXPERIENCE IS PERMANENT.', 145-155). BuildComposer.cs:166-174 lets a champion weave only AvailableSkills() plus its signature. save.LearnedSkills now only records which skills you have ever seen, so the Build screen can name them; it grants no access (Game1.cs:1186-1195, 1543-1546). Skill levels do stay (SkillProgress 'Levels are never lost'). The replacement is accurate and plain.

claim: Its copy is the current one (conquest at wave twenty, checkpoints paid in Memory Dust, trait points, five classes). [line 29: '... the six forms ...']

The strip file is still called forms.png, but its alt text in description.html reads 'The six styles'. The other items check out: conquest is at wave 20 and checkpoints cost 25 Dust per skipped wave (Checkpoints.cs:29, 35). The replacement is fine. claim: Twelve skills across six styles ... each carrying a SOURCE, and each deepened by a variation and two of its three reinforcements as it levels from use.
evidence: There are 12 SHARED skills, one active and one passive per style (SkillCatalogue.cs:390-751). But SkillCatalogue.All holds 22 entries, because there are also 10 SIGNATURE skills, one per champion (SkillCatalogue.cs:804-1105, OwnerCharacterId; CharacterRoster.cs SignatureSkillId). A reviewer who counts the catalogue will doubt 'twelve'. 'A variation and two of three' is correct: SkillProgress.MaxLevel = 3 since 2026-09-09 (SkillProgress.cs:43-67). A skill's Source comes from its chosen variation (SkillCatalogue.cs:120-125).
replacement: Twelve shared skills across six styles — HAMMER crushes, VOLLEY rains, SNARE answers, SIGN amplifies, FIELD ticks, DRAIN feeds — and one signature skill for each champion. As a skill levels from use, you choose one of its two variations, which gives it a SOURCE. Then you choose two of that variation's three reinforcements.
note: The evidence holds. SkillCatalogue.All has 22 entries: 12 shared skills plus 10 signature skills, one per champion, each with OwnerCharacterId. Signature skills have their own style, variations and reinforcements, and sit in a slot that cannot be removed (PlayerLoadout.SignatureSlot), so every player sees one. 'Twelve skills' leaves out a feature every player meets. 'Each carrying a SOURCE' describes the old model; the chosen variation now gives the Source. 'A variation and two of its three reinforcements' is right (MaxLevel = 3). The replacement is accurate and clearer.

claim: Add Vows — rules you accept for extra power that only pay while your build keeps the rule
evidence: 11 of the 13 vows are Demand vows and pay only while the rule holds. Two are StaticCost vows, VOW OF FRAGILITY and RECKLESS OFFERING (Builds/Vows.cs:585-599). Those two always pay and always cost you something: IsActive returns true for StaticCost (Vows.cs:621-624).
replacement: Add Vows — rules you accept for extra power. Most pay only while your build keeps the rule. Two always pay, and always cost you something.
note: Confirmed. VOW OF FRAGILITY and RECKLESS OFFERING are StaticCost vows (Vows.cs:585, 599). Their text reads 'ALWAYS ON', and IsActive returns true for StaticCost (Vows.cs:624). So 'only pay while your build keeps the rule' is false for 2 of the 13. The replacement is accurate. README line 24 repeats the same phrase, which is outside this finding.

claim: When it falls, it gets back up and pushes on. Nothing is banked, nothing is lost.
evidence: A fall does not continue the same descent. It starts a new one with a fresh champion: 'A NEW DESCENT IS A NEW CHAMPION' (Expeditions/Descent.cs:119-148, after DownedSeconds = 1.6, Descent.cs:55). The new descent starts at Math.Max(StartWave, FreeStartWave), which means wave 1 or a checkpoint paid for in Dust (HuntScreen.cs:1369-1406). The rest of the sentence is correct: every wave pays when it clears (Descent.cs:172-177), so nothing earned is lost. The same sentence is in docs/store/itch/description.html.
replacement: When it falls, it gets back up and starts again, from the first wave or from a checkpoint you paid for. What it earned stays earned.
note: Confirmed. A fall does not continue the same descent. HuntScreen.StartRun mints a new champion ('A NEW DESCENT IS A NEW CHAMPION') and starts at Math.Max(StartWave, FreeStartWave) (HuntScreen.cs:1406). StartWave is the checkpoint, which costs Dust on every descent. FreeStartWave is a one-time resume after time away, used for one descent only (HuntScreen.cs:326-334). So after a fall, the next descent starts at wave 1 or at a paid checkpoint. Every wave pays as soon as it clears (Descent.PushWave), so 'what it earned stays earned' is right. The replacement is accurate. description.html has the same sentence.

claim: Warren: idle production of three currencies while you are away (also line 43: 'Facilities produce Gleam, Memory Dust and Forge materials')
evidence: The Warren makes FOUR resources: WarrenResource { Gleam, Dust, Scrap, Essence } (Warrens/Warren.cs:16). The eight facilities split into 2 Gleam, 2 Dust, 2 Scrap and 2 Essence (Warren.cs:67-77). 'Three currencies' only works if Scrap and Essence count as one. The Warren opens on the first conquest (Unlocks.cs:189), and more facilities open with each conquest (Warren.cs:75, 2 + conquered).
replacement: - Warren: eight facilities make Gleam, Memory Dust and Forge materials, while you play and while you are away. (Leave line 44 as it is: 'Forge materials' already covers Scrap and Essence.)

'Three currencies' is left over from the Gleam/Insight/Dust Warren; INSIGHT was cut on 2026-08-31, and the old warren.png still shows it. So the line 58 bullet is wrong. Line 44, 'Gleam, Memory Dust and Forge materials', is already correct, because Scrap and Essence are the Forge materials, and it is plainer for a store reader. It does not need to change. Also, the Warren produces during play as well as while you are away (Game1.TickWarren runs every frame once the Warren is open).

claim: Turkish short description block (implies a Turkish-reading audience can play)
evidence: The game has no Turkish interface. A search of src finds no localisation or language setting, and all UI strings are English literals (e.g. Unlocks.cs:211-271). The current itch copy ends its Turkish block with 'Türkçe arayüz yolda.' (docs/store/itch/description.html). This block does not, so a Turkish reader could expect a Turkish game.
replacement: > Çevrimdışı bir idle otomatik-savaş oyunu. Şampiyonun dalgaları kendi başına temizler — oyun kapalıyken bile. Kılıcı sen sallamazsın: build'i sen örer, ekipmanı sen dövmede işler, dünya zorlaştıkça hangi yolu yürüyeceğine sen karar verirsin. Oyun şimdilik yalnızca İngilizce; Türkçe arayüz yolda.
note: The mismatch is real. The game has no Turkish interface (no localisation code; all UI strings are English literals). The Turkish block (line 24) describes the game in Turkish and never says it is English only. The live itch copy (description.html) ends its Turkish block with 'Türkçe arayüz yolda.', and line 68 of this doc says 'Turkish to follow', so the promise matches the stated plan. The replacement's Turkish is correct. The replacement abbreviates the unchanged text with '...', so the full line is given below.
